Title: Qud Expanded Community Edition
Description:
[h1]Qud Expanded Community Edition[/h1]
[i]A community-maintained fork of [b]Caves of Qud Expanded[/b] by Mura.[/i]

This is a [b]separate mod[/b]. It does not replace, modify, or take over the original, which remains Mura's and is still available here:
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1134036260]Caves of Qud Expanded[/url]

[h1]Development note[/h1]
I, VixyGrey, do use AI to help me with development and documentation tasks.

[h1]What the mod does[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Psionic Adept[/b] — a third genotype with 18 subtypes, split between casters and martial guardians.
[*][b]Psionic chips[/b] — 144 implantable chips that grant real, working mutations to genotypes that cannot mutate. All of them can now be found.
[*][b]Complete weapon and armor families[/b] — every tier from bronze to zetachrome, one-handed and two-handed, with consistent stats and prices.
[*][b]New weapon classes[/b] — katanas, rapiers, halberds, greataxes, greatswords, war hammers, wristblades and more.
[*][b]Skill and economy retuning[/b], and a home base building in Joppa.
[/list]

[h1]Compatibility[/h1]
This fork treats compatibility as a hard requirement. Every change to a vanilla record is a merge rather than a replacement, so the mod does not silently overwrite vanilla data or fight other mods, and it does not discard what future Qud patches add. That is enforced automatically on every change.

[h1]One thing this fork removed[/h1]
Multiweapon Fighting no longer offers Akimbo. Akimbo is unchanged and still available in the Pistol tree, where it has always lived, and Multiweapon Fighting keeps this mod's reduced stat requirements for Expertise and Mastery.

The two powers shared a single implementation, and Qud maps each implementation to exactly one power. That meant this mod's copy was served wherever the game asked for the vanilla one — most visibly on the [b]Gunslinger[/b] calling, which grants Akimbo by implementation name and so displayed the wrong power.

None of this was apparent for years, because both powers were called "Akimbo" and looked identical wherever they appeared. It only surfaced when this fork renamed one of them while working on something unrelated. Giving the mod's version its own implementation fixed the Gunslinger, but a character who bought both then ended up with the ability listed twice and a skills screen that would not close — so the power was removed rather than shipped with a known way to spoil a run.

Removing it costs nothing you cannot get elsewhere, and it restores vanilla's behaviour for every character, including ones who never touch Multiweapon Fighting.

[h1]Requires a new character[/h1]
Some identifiers changed during the fork, and Qud writes those into save files. [b]Start a new character with this mod enabled.[/b] Saves from the original mod are not compatible.
